about: Values from official and peer-reviewed sources: the regulatory definitions behind the model's constants (tests/test_constants.py ties each constant to its quote), the auxiliary load (the only model input not measured on the cars themselves), the climate-control powers shown for orientation, and values that cross-check the EPA certificates (data/epa_certification.json). Each value carries a verbatim quote from its source, or the spreadsheet cell it was read from; tools/verify_references.py checks every one against the fingerprinted document. Download the documents into data/sources/ to re-run the check.

charging_efficiency.quote: Battery charging efficiency can vary, but it is often 84% to 93%
The charging efficiency is calculated using the battery energy EB as well as the charged energy EC.
The best value is achieved by charging with all three phases at a maximum charging current of 16 A. Here, the charging process achieves an efficiency of 87.21%.
The lowest efficiency is achieved with a low current of 10 A and single-phase charging. This results in a mean efficiency for the charging of 79.58%.
The coloumns represent the charging current from 6 A to 32 A.
